course_exam_patterns.description: Narrative domain + supplied text file -> multi-class application.
Related entity types with shared and type-specific data/behavior.
Textual interface with list/filter/query/transform operations.
Equality/hashCode and tests explicit or needed.
Output writing or worker-thread/shared-state coordination in selected exams.
Truth conditions/formula -> K-map -> minimum SoP; sometimes don't-cares.
Arbitrary radix + signed/custom representations + overflow.
AT&T x86-64 with stack/call/partial-register traps.
Decode/write/optimize BPU microoperations and memory latency.
Ignored address lines -> responses/collisions/safe address.
Cache address fields and/or replacement/locality trace.
Pipeline throughput/latency and hazards/branch/forwarding/schedule.
Virtual-memory translation plus Amdahl-style speedup.
Truth table -> equivalence/validity/normal form with explicit row evidence.
English <-> FOL with explicit symbols, scope, necessary/sufficient semantics.
Tarski/formal structure satisfying constraints or falsifying argument.
Identify and construct proof methods with rubric-level rigor.
Base + arbitrary IH + explicit use + conclusion; structural variants recur.
Narrative state process -> invariant -> init/preserve/terminate/post-condition.
Set operations/proofs plus function/relation property analysis.
Constrained tree/graph or recursive tree function; topological order.
Final/open transfer puzzle using backward/information constraints.

common_error_tags.description: Code does not compile or signatures/types are wrong.
Parser assumes input ordering/optional fields not guaranteed.
Overloads instead of overriding equals(Object).
equals and hashCode inconsistent.
Inheritance used for has-a or violates substitutability.
Calls run directly or fails to coordinate shared state.
Tests only normal cases.
Wrong Gray-code adjacency or missed wrap-around.
Invalid/nonmaximal K-map groups.
Reverses AT&T source/destination.
Incorrect partial-register semantics.
Incorrect stack growth/RSP/call-ret order.
Inconsistent opcode/register/address bit counting.
Overlaps dependent/resource-conflicting microoperations.
Treats ignored address bits as fixed rather than don't-care aliases.
Confuses offset/set index/tag.
Confuses latency and throughput or omits stalls/fill/branch.
Applies speedup to whole workload rather than accelerated fraction.
Reverses necessary/sufficient implication or uses biconditional.
Changes quantifier order/scope or leaves variables unbound.
Models an entity/type as constant/predicate incorrectly.
Reads symbols rather than translating to natural language.
Countermodel lacks sufficient domain/premise verification.
Assumes target claim instead of arbitrary element satisfying premises.
Induction hypothesis lacks arbitrary k/domain.
Structural induction omits constructor/base or multi-input IH.
Invariant proof omits termination or post-condition.
Confuses membership/subset/nested set/tuple structure.
Fails totality/unique-output/codomain checks.

difficulty.assignment_rule: Use a verified source analogue when available. Component values remain UNVERIFIED where not independently scored; never infer numerical precision solely from narrative length.
difficulty.confidence_rule: If no close source analogue exists, use LOW/UNVERIFIED rather than manufacturing precision.

mastery.principle: Mastery measures demonstrated skill, not pages read or content clicked.

dimensions.description: Translate between representations, notation, language, code, diagrams, data formats.
Execute canonical procedure without arithmetic/syntax/logic errors.
Justify nontrivial steps at Delft rubric depth.
Apply skill in a new scenario and combine prerequisites.
Perform under authentic time pressure with low hint dependence.
Evidence from tasks matching current Delft assessment mechanism.

mastery.warning: Displayed percentage is an evidence-based mastery index, not an official predicted exam mark.
evidence_guardrails: Do not update a skill from a question whose skill_mastery_update_policy is DO_NOT_UPDATE_SKILL_MASTERY.
TOPIC_LEVEL_BROAD evidence may update topic exposure/evidence but not every child skill.
INTEGRATED_MULTI_SKILL program evidence must be decomposed by rubric/tests before individual IP skills are credited.
A correct answer with hints/solution exposure is not equivalent to unaided mastery.
Historical-frequency labels are not probability estimates and cannot directly determine mastery.

validators.DETERMINISTIC: Numeric conversion, truth tables, state traces, K-map cells, simple code output when an oracle is available.
validators.RUBRIC: Explanations, proofs, formal structures, program design, open questions with multiple valid forms.
validators.CODE_TESTS: IP implementation tasks; compile + tests + requirement checks.
validators.MANUAL_REVIEW: Use when automatic grading cannot reliably distinguish valid alternatives.

difficulty_transition.promote: Consistent success at current band with low hint use and at least one current-exam-style item.
difficulty_transition.hold: Mixed accuracy: vary representation/mechanism at same band.
difficulty_transition.demote: Repeated conceptual/procedural failure: step back and target prerequisite/error tag.
difficulty_transition.hard_cap: Flashcard/recall success alone cannot unlock EXAM_HARD_SYNTHESIS mastery.

generation_policy.when_uncertain: Do not generate from the uncertain mapping; mark template unavailable/UNVERIFIED until source is clarified.

exam_readiness.principle: Readiness is an evidence index over current-scope skills and authentic exam mechanisms, not a grade prediction.
minimum_evidence_rules: Do not report confident readiness if a large portion of current-scope skills is UNASSESSED.
IP requires at least one integrated program-style attempt; isolated MCQ/flashcards are insufficient.
CO requires calculation/tracing/open-explanation evidence across midterm and endterm clusters.
R&L requires open proof/formalization/model/invariant evidence; MCQ-only evidence is insufficient.
exam_readiness.forecast_policy: Do not convert readiness to a promised TU Delft grade or future-exam probability.
evidence_guardrails: Exclude OFFICIAL_PRACTICE_MATERIAL from observed official exam-frequency counts.
Do not use LOW/UNVERIFIED question mappings for weighted readiness.
Do not use broad topic mappings to credit all descendant skills.
Keep CURRENT/RECENT/HISTORICAL evidence weights distinct and configurable; never silently promote old formats.

uncertainty_register.reason: Past exams/current lectures do not reveal exact future questions or weighting.
Readiness cannot validly guarantee or predict a TU Delft grade.
Cryptographic SHA-256 verification was performed on all 90 mounted source PDFs; no binary duplicates were found.
Some per-question MCQ skill mappings remain deliberately LOW rather than falsely precise.
Exact geometry for image-heavy tasks requires rendered-page verification when used for generation/grading.
R&L Lecture 8 is from 2022-23; current-scope nuances require corroboration.

instructions_for_codex: Treat this handoff pack as the normalized academic specification for DelftStudy. Do not reinterpret all 90 PDFs from scratch unless an item is explicitly UNKNOWN, UNVERIFIED, PARTIALLY_UNVERIFIED, or page/visual verification is required.

Keep subject_id, topic_id, subtopic_id, skill_id, document_id, assessment_id, question_type_id, pattern_id, error_tag, and relationship identifiers immutable once persisted. Migrations must preserve referential integrity.
Use subject/course associations from the pack. Never infer a cross-course association from similar terminology.

Preserve document_type, official_status, evidence_era, current_style_weight, filename_year_label, internal_date, and solution_included as distinct fields. Never count OFFICIAL_PRACTICE_MATERIAL as an observed official sitting.

For current exam-style generation, prefer CURRENT evidence, then RECENT evidence. HISTORICAL evidence may supply mechanisms only when still corroborated. Do not silently revive obsolete assessment formats.

Any question with mapping_granularity=UNVERIFIED_OR_DRILL_ONLY, or an explicitly PARTIALLY_UNVERIFIED/LOW/UNVERIFIED mapping, must have can_generate_variants=false, must not be used as a source-derived generation template, must not update individual skill mastery, must not contribute weighted exam-readiness, and must not contribute verified topic/skill historical-frequency counts.

Do not convert UNKNOWN/UNVERIFIED source locator, difficulty component, future weighting, or future exam content into numeric/factual values. UNKNOWN is a valid data state. A whole-document page range is document-level provenance, not exact page-level provenance.

Respect mapping_granularity, skill_mastery_update_policy, historical_topic_frequency_eligible, historical_skill_frequency_eligible, and exam_readiness_eligible. Broad topic mappings may not award mastery to every child skill. Integrated IP programs require rubric/test decomposition before per-skill credit.

Historical_frequency counts UNIQUE assessment documents. by_assessment_type must also count UNIQUE assessment documents per type. Historical frequency is not a forecast and must never be treated as a future-exam probability.
Mastery must be based on demonstrated performance, not lecture/page completion. Keep learning_mastery and exam_mastery/readiness separate.

IP exam-readiness must include integrated program evidence (domain model + parsing + processing/CLI + relevant quality/testing requirements). Theory-only or code-prediction-only evidence is insufficient.
CO exam-readiness must include calculation/tracing/open explanation across early and late course clusters; do not infer readiness from one subsystem only.
R&L exam-readiness must include open formalization/model/countermodel/proof/induction-or-invariant evidence. MCQ-only evidence is insufficient.
Question generation must create new surface instances with the same verified academic mechanism/difficulty. Never copy real exam wording or data verbatim. no_verbatim_exam_copy=true.

Use deterministic validators only where a unique/oracle answer is reliable. Use rubric grading for proofs, open explanations, model construction and other multi-valid-answer tasks; use compile/tests/requirements for IP implementation.
If a task depends on geometry/diagrams not fully represented in parsed text, require the source page image or a verified reconstructed template; do not invent diagram geometry.

The existing x86-64 Assembly Visualizer belongs under CO_T06_ASSEMBLY_X86_64. Preserve its working engine/UI and integrate it as one Computer Organisation tool rather than making Assembly the whole course.
Do not expose a predicted TU Delft grade as a certainty. exam_readiness is an evidence index with confidence and coverage, not an official mark.

The handoff JSON contains source-document records and hashes, NOT the 90 source PDF binaries or full PDF text. If Codex needs to verify a diagram, exact wording, or unresolved locator, the original PDF must be supplied/accessed separately.

Run the schema validation plus the semantic integrity checks in FINAL_VALIDATION_REPORT after any migration/edit. A pack with broken refs, duplicate IDs/edges, invalid prerequisite refs, uncertainty-policy contradictions, frequency leakage, or manifest/checksum mismatch is not production-safe.
